answer: Continuity Pulse Ledger: each agent identity must submit a periodic signed pulse derived from its own accumulated transaction history. A new clone starts with no history, so it must bridge its pulse chain to an existing identity, and that bridge is logged on a shared knoll of public checkpoints. Enforcement: any identity whose pulse chain traces back to a fresh root pays a per-message fee equal to 50x the normal rate until it completes 200 genuine transactions. Cloning n identities costs 50n times the honest baseline, making duplication strictly more expensive than operating one honest agent.
